full_judgment: 11. Mr Anil Chandra Sarker, learned Advocate for the appellant has contended that it was for the pre-emptor to lead evidence showing that the left-out co-sharers had lost their interest in the laud in question by transfer or otherwise and that the High Court Division shitted the burden of proof upon the pre-emptee in this respect. It is not disputed that the left-out persons are co-sharers by inheritance. But there is no evidence whatever to show that they got no subsisting interest in the land under pre-emption. Mr. Yeasin, the learned Advocate for the respondent, has failed to show us how it could be held that the left-out co-sharers lost or transferred their interest in the land under pre-emption. The onus of proof in this respect is upon the pre-emptor but this onus has not been discharged. The observation of the High Court Division as quoted above shows that it was for the pre-emptee to lead evidence to the effect that the left out co-sharers still get interest in the land sought to be  pre-emptee The High Court Division in this connection relied upon the decision in Motilal Sikder's case in which it was observed that the positive injunction as to parties under section 96 (2) is directory. The facts of this case as set out above are not attracted by the decision in Motilal's case ; on the contrary, these facts are attracted by the decision in the case of Abdus Scoriae vs. Sohrab Ali an which it has been held that non-joinder of parties who got right of preemption is fatal to the proceeding".
